document.title: Lazy CJK fallback via Droid Sans Fallback Full
document.summary: The glyph cache gains a third fallback font, Droid Sans Fallback Full, which the font registry opens on the first character the requested font and DejaVu Sans both lack. The VPK ships the font, the smoke golden draws Japanese and Chinese, and the glossary names it the Runtime Fallback Font.
document.why: Issue #50 asks for full Unicode text; the approved [revised proposal](source:s1) falls back from the requested font to DejaVu Sans to a bundled CJK font, with the CJK font loading on first miss.

sources.title: Fonts: non-ASCII glyphs, size-independent atlases, package fonts on buttons
sources.gist: Revised proposal: dynamic glyph cache, DejaVu Sans then Droid Sans Fallback Full as fallbacks, Twemoji colour emoji; three PRs.

lookFor: Droid Sans Fallback Full has no Hangul syllables, so Korean still draws DejaVu's missing-glyph box; the [proposal](source:s1) does not mention this, and the smoke line uses `日本語 かな 中文` instead of Korean.
The vendored AOSP 7.1.2 build is 4.0 MB, not the 4.5 MB the [proposal](source:s1) estimates; the larger AOSP 4.4 build also lacks Hangul.

groups.title: Three-font fallback chain in the glyph cache
groups.why: The [proposal](source:s1) puts a CJK font after DejaVu Sans and loads it on first miss.
groups.summary: `glyph_cache_get` walks the requested font, the fallback, then the font `glyph_cache_set_fallback_loader`'s callback opens once, and the harness checks each link plus the single lazy load.
lookFor: Subtle: any codepoint both earlier fonts lack opens the 4 MB font, not only CJK; a private-use character such as U+E000 in a Latin-only app triggers the load once.
A loader that returns NULL is consumed anyway, so a missing font file logs one warning and later misses go straight to the missing-glyph box.

groups.title: Font registry owns and ships the Runtime Fallback Font
groups.why: The chain needs a loader that owns the font, and the device needs the file in the VPK.
groups.summary: `load_fallback_font` in `fonts.c` opens `assets/fonts/DroidSansFallbackFull.ttf` for the glyph cache and frees it at shutdown, and `CMakeLists.txt` packs it with its Apache-2.0 licence into the VPK and `upload_vita`.

groups.title: Smoke golden draws CJK
groups.why: The golden proves the fallback renders real glyphs on Linux.
groups.summary: The smoke header gets a `日本語 かな 中文` line beside the Hungarian text, and the Linux golden is refreshed to match.

groups.title: Glossary and SDK README
groups.why: The [proposal](source:s1) adds the Runtime Fallback Font term to CONTEXT.md.
groups.summary: `CONTEXT.md` adds **Runtime Fallback Font** and rewrites the Deck App Font, Runtime Default Font and fallback entries in place for the three-font chain, and the SDK README names the CJK coverage in one sentence.

commits.subject: feat(ui): lazy CJK fallback after the Runtime Default Font
commits.author: Máté Molnár
commits.body:
Glyphs fall back from the requested font to DejaVu Sans to Droid Sans Fallback Full, which opens on the first character the first two lack, so Latin-only apps keep today's startup and memory. The VPK and upload_vita ship the font.
